decisions.reason: Because the net price display plugin is close to the firm's core online-shop customization work and the firm has its own R&D, management is likely to see enough related knowledge to improve it rather than withdraw it.

An ERP system interface plugin builds directly on the firm's established integration capabilities and supports its move toward broader multichannel commerce, so absorptive capacity arguments favor retaining it.

A price comparison tracking plugin fits the firm's analytics and performance-marketing knowledge base, and with in-house R&D in a growing market the firm is more likely to refine it than drop it, though overlap in the portfolio raises a little risk.

This price comparison tracking plugin is close to the firm's existing optimization and advertising offer, so management should be able to learn from early market feedback and keep it unless portfolio overlap becomes a reason to consolidate.

Since the product remains near the firm's established e-commerce analytics expertise and the firm is hiring and conducting its own R&D, it is more likely to stay on the market than be discontinued, despite some chance of internal consolidation.

The net price reporting plugin is a close extension of the firm's reporting and shop-support activities, and the firm's own R&D increases its ability to assimilate user feedback and commercialize improvements.
